basis: Inflammation of mesenteric lymph nodes, usually infectious; mesenteric location alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Defining skeletal/dental defects and microcephaly; hypomyelination 1/2. Cardiac hypertrophy/conduction disease 1/2; fat loss and insulin resistance (1/2 each) omitted by cap.
Defined by skeletal muscle fiber dysfunction; additional organs depend on the specific myopathy.
Occlusion directly affects arteries; downstream organ injury varies with the artery and is not universal across this umbrella.
CRX-related congenital retinal dystrophy with severe visual impairment and absent electroretinographic responses.
Microcephaly and cleft palate define the syndrome and occur in 80-99%; retinal changes and finger contractures occur in only 5-29%.
Immune-mediated inflammatory arthritis and enthesitis; extra-articular damage is not established in at least 30% across the group.
Inherited hepatobiliary transport disorder causing intrahepatic cholestasis during pregnancy; pruritus does not establish direct skin damage.
Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor originating in the appendix; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Inherited platelet adhesion defect with macrothrombocytopenia and bleeding; bleeding sites do not establish additional organ disease.
Defined by impaired hearing; central auditory dysfunction occurs in a subset and does not justify neurologic labeling across the umbrella.
KCNJ13-related congenital retinal dystrophy; reduced visual acuity and cataracts are reported in 3/3 patients.
Developmental delay/ID 5/5; finger contractures 30-79% (2/5). Reflux and recurrent otitis are separate diagnoses; feeding difficulty alone does not establish GI damage.
Defined anatomical umbrella for ear, nose and throat disease; nose, pharynx and larynx belong to the pulmonary axis.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder with ventricular arrhythmias; syncope does not itself establish neurologic damage.
Renal magnesium/calcium wasting and nephrocalcinosis define this electrolyte transport disorder; severe ocular disease is subtype-specific, with pooled frequency unclear.
Familial cortical movement disorder with action myoclonus in 11/11; falls and insomnia do not establish damage to additional organs.
Cerebellar hypoplasia and retinal degeneration define the syndrome; visual impairment, optic atrophy and neurologic abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Inherited red-cell production failure; erythroid hypoplasia and anemia occur in 2/2 reported patients.
Carcinoma originates in nasal cavity glandular epithelium; the nasal airway belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Poikiloderma and cataracts 10/10; skeletal anomalies and dental defects 30-79%. Ovarian insufficiency (2/5 females) omitted by cap.
C1q-associated lupus commonly affects skin (~90%) and kidneys (~30-40%); joint involvement is less frequent than in typical SLE and is excluded.
Syngnathia is congenital jaw fusion, consistent with the dysostosis parent, directly restricting oral opening and feeding; other organ involvement is insufficiently specified.
Benign tumor originating in cardiac muscle; associated tuberous sclerosis is a separate disease, and respiratory symptoms do not establish lung damage.
Leukodystrophy affects brainstem and spinal pathways; optic disc pallor indicates optic nerve damage in 3/10 (~30%). Nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
